name: misinformation-interventions
label: Misinformation Interventions (v3.1)
description: Coding scheme for the misinformation-intervention meta-analysis: study metadata, sample, open-science and design, the intervention modules, and the per-contrast effect sizes.

fields.name: Study_ID
fields.label: Study ID
fields.description: Unique ID string, [Author][Year]_Exp[1-9].
fields.instruction: Study_ID = first-author surname + year + `_ExpN`, ASCII only, e.g. `Austin2025_Exp1`, `Jolley2014_Exp9`; a two-study paper uses `_Exp1`, `_Exp2`. One record per trial/experiment, and the record's `DV_Metrics` hold that experiment's own contrasts.

fields.name: Parent_Study_ID
fields.label: Parent Study ID
fields.description: Study_ID of the record one level up in the hierarchy (experiment -> paper/study). Null for a top-level record.  The per-record aggregation level was removed on 2026-09-17; every extraction record now describes one experiment and carries its own DV contrasts.
fields.instruction: Bookkeeping key - no source span required. Leave it null for a top-level record: every record now describes one experiment and carries its own DV contrasts.

fields.name: Year
fields.label: Publication Year
fields.description: Publication year.
fields.instruction: Metadata field: read the publication year from page 1 of the paper (the title block or the citation line).

fields.name: Publication
fields.label: Publication
fields.description: Merged publication form (one moderator). Controlled vocabulary: paper_peer_reviewed, paper_unreviewed, thesis, dissertation, preprint, working_paper, conference_paper, unpublished_manuscript, report. Splits `paper` into peer-reviewed vs unreviewed.
fields.instruction: Metadata field: read the publication form from page 1 (the journal line, the thesis statement or the preprint banner). Use only the codes in the options list.

fields.name: DOI
fields.label: DOI
fields.description: Digital Object Identifier, or null.
fields.instruction: Metadata field: read the DOI from page 1 (the header, the first-page footer or the journal citation line). Leave it null when the paper prints no DOI.

fields.name: Authors
fields.label: Authors
fields.description: Author names (Last, First), semicolon-separated.
fields.instruction: Metadata field: read the author list from page 1 and write it as `Last, First; Last, First`.

fields.name: Title
fields.label: Title
fields.description: Title of the paper.
fields.instruction: Metadata field: read the title from page 1, verbatim.

fields.name: Study_Description
fields.label: Study Description
fields.description: 2-sentence description of the study design and primary aim.
fields.instruction: Required on every record. Write two sentences describing the study design and the primary aim, taken from the paper's abstract and method section. Bookkeeping key - no source span required.

fields.name: N_Recruited
fields.label: N Recruited
fields.description: Number of participants recruited before exclusions, or null.
fields.instruction: A table-based numeric field: mark the table cell/row (or the participant-flow sentence) that reports how many were recruited before exclusions. Leave it null when the paper does not state it.

fields.name: N_Analyzed
fields.label: N Analyzed
fields.description: Final analyzed sample size, or null.
fields.instruction: A table-based numeric field: mark the table cell/row (or the participant-flow sentence) that reports the final analysed sample. Leave it null when the paper does not state the analysed N.

fields.name: N_Reported_Per_Condition
fields.label: N Reported Per Condition
fields.description: 1=cell sizes explicitly reported, 0=not reported (must be inferred), null=unclear.
fields.instruction: 1 = the paper reports the cell size of every condition explicitly, 0 = the cell sizes must be inferred, null = unclear. When you set 0, say in Rationale_Notes how the cell sizes were obtained.

fields.name: N_Inference_Method
fields.label: N Inference Method
fields.description: 1=Reported, 2=Equal split of total N, 3=Other (specify in Rationale_Notes).
fields.instruction: 1 = the cell sizes are reported, 2 = an equal split of the total N was assumed, 3 = another derivation - then specify it in Rationale_Notes.

fields.name: Age_Mean
fields.label: Mean Age
fields.description: Numeric mean age, or null (leave null when only a median/range/category is reported).
fields.instruction: A table-based numeric field: mark the table cell/row that reports the mean age. Leave it null when the paper reports only a median, a range or a category.

fields.name: Age_SD
fields.label: Age SD
fields.description: Standard deviation of age, or null.
fields.instruction: A table-based numeric field: mark the table cell/row that reports the SD of age; null when the paper reports only the mean.

fields.name: Age_Reported_As
fields.label: Age Reported As
fields.description: 1=Mean/SD, 2=Median/Range, 3=Categorical band, 4=Not reported.
fields.instruction: 1 = mean/SD, 2 = median/range, 3 = categorical band, 4 = not reported. This field says how the paper reports age; Age_Mean and Age_SD carry the numbers.

fields.name: Age_Group
fields.label: Age Group
fields.description: 1=Children, 2=Adolescents, 3=Adults, 4=Mixed. Null if cannot be determined.
fields.instruction: 1 = children, 2 = adolescents, 3 = adults, 4 = mixed. Derive it from the sample the paper describes; null when it cannot be determined.

fields.name: Gender_Ratio
fields.label: Gender Ratio
fields.description: Object mapping gender labels to percentages or counts, e.g. {"female": 59, "male": 40, "non-binary": 1}; null if not reported.
fields.instruction: A table-based numeric field: mark the table cell/row that reports the gender breakdown, and write it as an object mapping the paper's own gender labels to the reported percentages or counts. Null if not reported.

fields.name: Gender_Reported_As
fields.label: Gender Reported As
fields.description: 1=Percentages, 2=Counts, 3=Not reported.
fields.instruction: 1 = the paper reports percentages, 2 = counts, 3 = not reported. Gender_Ratio carries the numbers.

fields.name: Covariates
fields.label: Covariates
fields.description: Array of objects listing variables controlled for, [{"covariate": string, "dv_name": string, "r_val": number|null}]. Empty array if none.
fields.instruction: A list-valued field: mark a passage that supports the listed values - one entry per variable the paper controlled for, with the DV it belongs to and the reported correlation when the paper gives one. Empty array if the paper controls for nothing.

fields.name: Country
fields.label: Countries
fields.description: Array of country strings, e.g. ["USA", "UK"]. Empty array if not reported.
fields.instruction: A list-valued field: mark a passage that supports the listed values - one country string per country the sample was drawn in. Empty array if the paper does not report the country.

fields.name: Sample_Region
fields.label: Sample Region
fields.description: Region/description when Country is not applicable (e.g. "international English-speaking", "Sub-Saharan Africa").
fields.instruction: A free-text field: write the region or description the paper gives where a country does not apply (e.g. 'international English-speaking', 'Sub-Saharan Africa'). Leave it empty when the paper does not report one - never invent a value.

fields.name: International_Sample
fields.label: International Sample
fields.description: 1=sample spans multiple countries, 0=single country, null=unclear.
fields.instruction: A boolean/derived coding: mark the sentence that states the underlying fact - the sample spans more than one country (1) or a single country (0). Null when the paper does not make it clear.

fields.name: WEIRD_Western
fields.label: WEIRD - Western
fields.description: 1=Western, 0=not, null=unclear.
fields.instruction: A boolean/derived coding: mark the sentence that states the underlying fact (the sample's Western status, or the country and region it comes from), not the code itself. Null when the paper does not make it clear.

fields.name: WEIRD_Educated
fields.label: WEIRD - Educated
fields.description: 1=Educated/high-education, 0=not, null=unclear.
fields.instruction: A boolean/derived coding: mark the sentence that states the underlying fact (the sample's education level, or the country and region it comes from), not the code itself. Null when the paper does not make it clear.

fields.name: WEIRD_Industrialized
fields.label: WEIRD - Industrialized
fields.description: 1=Industrialized, 0=not, null=unclear.
fields.instruction: A boolean/derived coding: mark the sentence that states the underlying fact (the sample's industrialized status, or the country and region it comes from), not the code itself. Null when the paper does not make it clear.

fields.name: WEIRD_Rich
fields.label: WEIRD - Rich
fields.description: 1=Rich/high-income, 0=not, null=unclear.
fields.instruction: A boolean/derived coding: mark the sentence that states the underlying fact (the sample's income status, or the country and region it comes from), not the code itself. Null when the paper does not make it clear.

fields.name: WEIRD_Democratic
fields.label: WEIRD - Democratic
fields.description: 1=Democratic, 0=not, null=unclear.
fields.instruction: A boolean/derived coding: mark the sentence that states the underlying fact (the sample's democratic status, or the country and region it comes from), not the code itself. Null when the paper does not make it clear.

fields.name: Setting
fields.label: Setting
fields.description: 1=Lab, 2=Field, 3=Classroom, 4=Online panel survey, 5=Online experiment, 6=Simulated field, 7=Other.
fields.instruction: Mark the sentence or the method section that states where the study ran: 1 lab, 2 field, 3 classroom, 4 online panel survey, 5 online experiment, 6 simulated field, 7 other.

fields.name: dataset_availability_status
fields.label: Dataset Availability Status
fields.description: 1=Open URL, 2=Upon request, 3=Not available, 4=Not stated.
fields.instruction: 1 = the paper gives an open URL, 2 = the data are available on request, 3 = the data are not available, 4 = not stated. An absence coding: for 4, mark the nearest relevant statement and say in Rationale_Notes that the paper contains no explicit statement.

fields.name: data_url
fields.label: Data URL
fields.description: Direct URL to the dataset, or null.
fields.instruction: A free-text field: copy the direct URL to the dataset exactly as the paper prints it. Leave it empty when there is none - never reconstruct a URL.

fields.name: data_repository
fields.label: Data Repository
fields.description: Repository name/ID (e.g. OSF ujwy3, Dryad, Zenodo), or null.
fields.instruction: A free-text field: name the repository and, where the paper gives one, its identifier (e.g. 'OSF ujwy3', 'Dryad', 'Zenodo'). Leave it empty when the paper names no repository.

fields.name: data_available
fields.label: Data Available (derived)
fields.description: Derived, not paper-coded: 1 when a harmonized participant-level dataset exists in `Datasets/<Study Key>/`, else 0. Populated by the reanalysis / analysis-suite scripts (`Scripts/suite_common.py:_data_available_map`).
fields.instruction: Not paper-coded: the pipeline sets this to 1 when a harmonized participant-level dataset exists in `Datasets/<Study Key>/` and to 0 otherwise. Leave it empty when you code.

fields.name: code_available
fields.label: Code Available
fields.description: 1=analysis code available, 0=not, null=not stated.
fields.instruction: 1 = the paper offers analysis code, 0 = it does not, null = not stated. A boolean/derived coding: mark the sentence that states the underlying fact (the availability statement, a repository link or the open-science badge).

fields.name: preregistration_status
fields.label: Preregistration Status
fields.description: 1=None, 2=Registered (no URL given), 3=Registered (URL given).
fields.instruction: 1 = no preregistration, 2 = registered but no URL given, 3 = registered with a URL. An absence coding: for 1, mark the nearest relevant statement (e.g. the open-science statement) and say in Rationale_Notes that the paper contains no explicit statement of a preregistration.

fields.name: preregistration_url
fields.label: Preregistration URL
fields.description: URL of the preregistration, or null.
fields.instruction: Copy the preregistration URL exactly as the paper prints it. Leave it empty when the paper registers without a URL (preregistration_status = 2) or does not register at all.

fields.name: ethics
fields.label: Ethics Approval
fields.description: 0=No mention, 1=Mentioned, 2=Institution named, 3=Institution and protocol number.
fields.instruction: 0 = the paper does not mention ethics, 1 = it mentions ethics approval, 2 = it names the institution, 3 = it gives the institution and the protocol number. Mark the sentence (or the ethics-approval footnote) that states it.

fields.name: consent_reported
fields.label: Consent Reported
fields.description: 1=informed consent reported, 0=not, null=not stated.
fields.instruction: 1 = the paper reports that informed consent was obtained, 0 = it does not, null = not stated. A boolean/derived coding: mark the sentence that states the underlying fact (the consent sentence in the participants or ethics section).

fields.name: n_arms
fields.label: Number of Arms
fields.description: Number of independent experimental groups/conditions.
fields.instruction: Count the independent experimental groups/conditions the experiment has, including the control arm. The number decides how many eligible primary contrasts the experiment can carry - one per intervention arm against the shared no-intervention control.

fields.name: design_factors
fields.label: Design Factors
fields.description: Array of manipulated factors, e.g. ["inoculation", "misinformation"] or ["credibility_badge", "social_norm"].
fields.instruction: A list-valued field: mark a passage that supports the listed values - one string per manipulated factor, e.g. ['inoculation', 'misinformation']. Empty array when the design is single-factor.

fields.name: factor_levels
fields.label: Factor Levels
fields.description: Array of objects, [{"factor": string, "levels": [string]}].
fields.instruction: A list-valued field: mark a passage that supports the listed values - one entry per factor with its levels, e.g. [{'factor': 'inoculation', 'levels': ['yes', 'no']}].

fields.name: within_between
fields.label: Within/Between
fields.description: 1=Between-subjects, 2=Within-subjects, 3=Mixed.
fields.instruction: 1 = between-subjects, 2 = within-subjects, 3 = mixed. Mark the sentence that states how participants were allocated.

fields.name: unit_of_analysis
fields.label: Unit of Analysis
fields.description: 1=Participant, 2=Item/headline, 3=Dyad/group, 4=Other.
fields.instruction: 1 = participant, 2 = item/headline, 3 = dyad/group, 4 = other. Mark the sentence that states the unit the analysis treats as the observation - and set 2 when the paper analyses headlines or claims as the data points.

fields.name: clustering
fields.label: Clustering
fields.description: Clustering/random effects structure, e.g. "standard errors clustered by post", or null.
fields.instruction: A free-text field: write the clustering/random-effects structure the paper uses, e.g. 'standard errors clustered by post'. Leave it empty when the paper does not state one - never invent a value.

fields.name: control_group_type
fields.label: Control Group Type
fields.description: 1=No-treatment/Passive, 2=Placebo (unrelated content), 3=Active (alternative intervention), 4=Waitlist, 5=Misinformation-only, 6=Other.
fields.instruction: 1 = no-treatment/passive, 2 = placebo (unrelated content), 3 = active (alternative intervention), 4 = waitlist, 5 = misinformation-only, 6 = other. Mark the sentence that describes the control arm. A contrast is eligible_primary = 1 only when this control receives no misinformation intervention of its own.

fields.name: Intervention_Type
fields.label: Intervention Type
fields.description: Multi-label list of intervention types from the merged vocabulary: inoculation, prebunking_warning, lateral_reading, credibility_labels, media_literacy_tips, fact_checking_training, openmindedness_intervention, debunking_and_rebuttals, community_correction, accuracy_prompts, friction, social_norms, platform_exposure_reduction, other. Multi-type experiments are allowed (e.g. ["inoculation", "friction"]). The former intervention_module field was removed on 2026-09-17; the module-specific coding fields are now implied by these types.
fields.instruction: A list-valued field: mark a passage that supports the listed values - one code per intervention the experiment delivers; a multi-type experiment is allowed. When the paper separates the components, keep the `Interventions[]` arms explicit and bind every DV to its arm with `Intervention_ID`.

fields.name: Intervention_Type_Detail
fields.label: Intervention Type Detail
fields.description: REQUIRED when Intervention_Type includes "other"; specify the combined/specific approach. Otherwise null.
fields.instruction: REQUIRED when Intervention_Type includes 'other': write the combined or specific approach the paper used. Otherwise leave it empty.

fields.name: Intervention_Topic
fields.label: Intervention Topic
fields.description: Topic or domain of the intervention (e.g. vaccines, climate change), or null.
fields.instruction: A free-text field: write the topic or domain the intervention addressed (e.g. vaccines, climate change). Leave it empty when the paper does not report one - never invent a value.

fields.name: Intervention_Duration
fields.label: Intervention Duration (minutes)
fields.description: Numeric duration of the intervention in minutes, or null.
fields.instruction: A table-based numeric field: mark the sentence or table cell that reports the exposure time in minutes. Leave it null when the paper does not state a duration.

fields.name: Modality
fields.label: Modality
fields.description: 1=Text, 2=Video, 3=Game/Gamified, 4=Mixed, 5=Other (specify in detail/notes), 6=Personal training.
fields.instruction: 1 = text, 2 = video, 3 = game/gamified, 4 = mixed, 5 = other (say which in the notes), 6 = personal training. Mark the method-section sentence that describes the delivery channel.

fields.name: Exposure_Schedule
fields.label: Exposure Schedule
fields.description: 1=Single massed session, 2=Spaced (multiple continuous sessions), 3=Boosted (delayed follow-up session).
fields.instruction: 1 = a single massed session, 2 = spaced over several continuous sessions, 3 = boosted (a delayed follow-up session). Mark the procedure-section sentence that describes the schedule.

fields.name: Pedagogy_Type
fields.label: Pedagogy Type
fields.description: 1=Direct Instruction, 2=Guided Inquiry, 3=Co-created/Collaborative.
fields.instruction: 1 = direct instruction, 2 = guided inquiry, 3 = co-created/collaborative. Mark the procedure sentence that describes how the material was taught.

fields.name: Instructor_Type
fields.label: Instructor Type
fields.description: 1=Researcher, 2=Teacher, 3=Peer, 4=Computer, 5=Anthropomorphic Agent, 6=Other.
fields.instruction: 1 = researcher, 2 = teacher, 3 = peer, 4 = computer, 5 = anthropomorphic agent, 6 = other. Mark the sentence that names who delivered the intervention.

fields.name: Feedback_Mechanics
fields.label: Feedback Mechanics
fields.description: 0=None, 1=Knowledge of Results (correct/incorrect), 2=Elaborated (explanation), 3=Forced Mastery.
fields.instruction: 0 = none, 1 = knowledge of results (correct/incorrect), 2 = elaborated (an explanation), 3 = forced mastery. Mark the procedure sentence that describes the feedback given during the intervention.

fields.name: Attention_Cues
fields.label: Attention Cues
fields.description: Array of applicable strings: ["Visual Signaling/Highlighting", "Explicit Ignore Instructions", "Physiological/Emotional Focus"].
fields.instruction: A list-valued field: mark a passage that supports the listed values - every cue the intervention used to hold attention: visual signalling/highlighting, explicit ignore instructions, physiological/emotional focus.

fields.name: Affective_Design
fields.label: Affective Design
fields.description: 0=Neutral, 1=Intentional Negative Trigger, 2=Humor/Positive Reinforcement.
fields.instruction: 0 = neutral, 1 = intentional negative trigger, 2 = humour/positive reinforcement. Mark the sentence that describes the affective framing of the intervention.

fields.name: Media_Support
fields.label: Media Support
fields.description: Array of applicable strings: ["Model teaching", "Visual aids"].
fields.instruction: A list-valued field: mark a passage that supports the listed values - the media supports the intervention used, e.g. ['Model teaching', 'Visual aids'].

fields.name: Comm_Strategies
fields.label: Communication Strategies
fields.description: Array of applicable strings: ["Interview techniques", "Sketching/narrative", "Verbal labelling"].
fields.instruction: A list-valued field: mark a passage that supports the listed values - the communication strategies used, e.g. ['Interview techniques', 'Sketching/narrative', 'Verbal labelling'].

fields.name: ICAP_Role
fields.label: ICAP Role
fields.description: 1=Passive, 2=Active, 3=Constructive, 4=Interactive.
fields.instruction: 1 = passive, 2 = active, 3 = constructive, 4 = interactive. Mark the sentence that describes how far the intervention made the learner engage with the material.

fields.name: Social_Context
fields.label: Social Context
fields.description: 1=Individual, 2=Prosocial, 3=Competitive.
fields.instruction: 1 = individual, 2 = prosocial, 3 = competitive. Mark the sentence that describes whether the intervention was done alone, in a prosocial setting or in a competitive one.

fields.name: Retrieval_Practice
fields.label: Retrieval Practice
fields.description: 0=Absent, 1=Present.
fields.instruction: 0 = absent, 1 = present. Mark the procedure sentence that shows whether the intervention made learners retrieve the material (e.g. practice tests, recall prompts).

fields.name: Contrasting_Cases
fields.label: Contrasting Cases
fields.description: 0=No, 1=Yes (manipulative vs. neutral examples).
fields.instruction: 0 = no, 1 = yes - the intervention contrasted manipulative with neutral examples. Mark the passage that shows the contrast.

fields.name: Concept_Labeling
fields.label: Concept Labeling
fields.description: 0=Implicit, 1=Explicit.
fields.instruction: 0 = implicit, 1 = explicit. Mark the passage that shows whether the intervention named the concept explicitly.

fields.name: Interleaving
fields.label: Interleaving
fields.description: 0=Blocked, 1=Interleaved.
fields.instruction: 0 = blocked, 1 = interleaved. Mark the passage that shows whether the material or the practice was mixed or blocked.

fields.name: Practice_Strategy
fields.label: Practice Strategy
fields.description: Array of applicable strings: ["Recall tests", "Easy-to-hard sequencing"].
fields.instruction: A list-valued field: mark a passage that supports the listed values - the practice strategies used, e.g. ['Recall tests', 'Easy-to-hard sequencing'].

fields.name: Self_Efficacy
fields.label: Self-Efficacy Support
fields.description: 0=No, 1=Yes (explicit support/indicators).
fields.instruction: 0 = no, 1 = yes - the intervention explicitly supported self-efficacy (e.g. mastery feedback, efficacy statements). Mark the passage that shows it.

fields.name: Synthetic
fields.label: Synthetic Stimuli
fields.description: 1=Synthetic, 2=Real, 3=Mixed.
fields.instruction: 1 = synthetic stimuli, 2 = real stimuli, 3 = mixed. Mark the method sentence that says how the stimuli were made.

fields.name: Stimuli
fields.label: Stimuli Type
fields.description: 1=Headlines, 2=Claims, 3=Source, 4=Headline+Claim, 5=Claim+Source, 6=Headline+Source, 7=Video, 8=Images, 9=Other.
fields.instruction: 1 = headlines, 2 = claims, 3 = source, 4 = headline+claim, 5 = claim+source, 6 = headline+source, 7 = video, 8 = images, 9 = other. Mark the stimuli-section sentence (or the table heading) that names the material.

fields.name: Stimuli_Topic
fields.label: Stimuli Topic
fields.description: Topic or domain of the stimuli, or null.
fields.instruction: A free-text field: write the topic or domain of the stimuli, e.g. vaccines, climate change. Leave it empty when the paper does not report one - never invent a value.

fields.name: Rationale_Notes
fields.label: Rationale Notes
fields.description: Brief note on inferred values, group-size inference, and effect-size conversions. Empty string if none.
fields.instruction: Record here every inference the paper does not state: the group-size inference and its method, the effect-size conversion and its assumption, the paper's silence on an absence coding, and any design fact the fields cannot carry (e.g. a fully-within design). Bookkeeping key - no source span required. Empty string when there is nothing to note.

fields.name: Fulltext_Exclusion_Criterion
fields.label: Full-text exclusion criterion (C1-C4)

options.label: insufficient reporting (study ran, but no eligible contrast is reported)
duplicate of an included study (non-independent report)

fields.description: Leave EMPTY when the study meets every inclusion criterion. Otherwise list the unmet criterion/criteria: C1 = No misinformation intervention; C2 = No control/comparison group; C3 = Not English; C4 = Not a primary experimental study. A study that fails a criterion is STILL fully coded, harmonized and reproduced as normal.
fields.instruction: Leave it EMPTY when the study meets every inclusion criterion. Otherwise list the unmet criterion/criteria and only those: C1 = no misinformation intervention, C2 = no control/comparison group, C3 = not English, C4 = not a primary experimental study. If the study meets C1-C4 but reports no eligible intervention-vs-control contrast (e.g. every arm is treated), leave the field empty and explain the design fact in Rationale_Notes - never write a label such as 'insufficient reporting' here. A failed criterion never excuses a thin coding: still code every experiment and every DV normally.

fields.name: Corresponding_Author_Name
fields.label: Corresponding author (name)
fields.description: Name of the author the paper directs correspondence to, e.g. "Jane Roe". Empty when the paper names no corresponding author. Recorded separately from the address in 'Corresponding_Author_Email'.
fields.instruction: The person the paper directs correspondence to, e.g. 'Jane Roe'; null when the paper names no corresponding author. A candidate counts only when the name is one of the paper's own authors, so an editor, a production office, a repository mailbox or an IRB contact is never mistaken for the contact. Bookkeeping key - no source span required.

fields.name: Corresponding_Author_Email
fields.label: Corresponding author (email)
fields.description: E-mail address of the corresponding author, as printed in the paper. Empty when no address is printed or none could be resolved to the corresponding author.
fields.instruction: The e-mail address as printed in the paper; null when no address is printed or none resolves to the corresponding author. Never invent an address from a domain pattern - null plus 'paper: no corresponding author named' is the correct answer for a paper that prints no address.

fields.name: Corresponding_Author_Source
fields.label: Corresponding author (source)
fields.description: Where the corresponding author was read from, e.g. "pdf: correspondence note, p. 1" or "openalex: corresponding_author_ids".
fields.instruction: Where the contact was read from, e.g. 'pdf: correspondence note, p. 1', 'openalex: corresponding_author_ids', or 'paper: no corresponding author named' when the paper names none. All three corresponding-author fields are record-level and appear on every record.

fields.name: Fully_Within
fields.label: Fully within (single arm)
fields.description: True when the experiment has no control arm, so it is excluded from every pooled product by default.
fields.instruction: Set it true when the experiment has no control arm at all (every arm is treated, or a single-arm pre-post design). A fully-within experiment is excluded from every pooled product by default, and its within-person pre-post change is coded as contrast_type = 4. Record the design fact in Rationale_Notes.

fields.name: dv_name
fields.label: DV Name
fields.description: Name/label of the dependent variable.
fields.instruction: Name the dependent variable as the paper names it, e.g. 'Accuracy (true minus false headlines)'. One row per distinct contrast x outcome x timepoint, so the name may repeat across rows; keep it recognisable.

fields.name: dv_domain
fields.label: DV Domains
fields.description: Controlled multi-label list: technique_recognition, credibility, sharing_intention, search_behavior, attitude_policy, trust, media_literacy_attitudes, critical_thinking, other.  The former levels echo_chamber, information_overload, social_norms, behavioral_choice and general_transfer were merged into "other" on 2026-09-17; confidence and affect were merged into "other", engagement_behavior into "sharing_intention", and belief_accuracy into "credibility" on 2026-09-19.
fields.instruction: Controlled list: technique_recognition, credibility, sharing_intention, search_behavior, attitude_policy, trust, media_literacy_attitudes, critical_thinking, other. Do not code confidence, certainty or metacognition as a dv_domain - they are a separate strand that is never pooled, so they belong in 'other'.

fields.name: score_types
fields.label: Score Types
fields.description: Controlled multi-label list: separate_true, separate_false, separate_manipulative, separate_nonmanipulative, discernment_difference, composite, signal_detection_auc, signal_detection_d_prime, signal_detection_c, dichotomous_accuracy, continuous_accuracy, proportion, proportion_difference, behavioral_choice, other, count, single_item, behavioral_intention, change_score, signal_detection_other.
fields.instruction: Controlled list: separate_true, separate_false, separate_manipulative, separate_nonmanipulative, discernment_difference, composite, signal_detection_auc, signal_detection_d_prime, signal_detection_c, dichotomous_accuracy, continuous_accuracy, proportion, proportion_difference, behavioral_choice, other, count, single_item, behavioral_intention, change_score. Use separate_true / separate_false when the paper reports a score per stimulus veracity, and discernment_difference when the DV is the difference between them.

fields.name: discernment_defined_as
fields.label: Discernment Defined As
fields.description: How a difference/discernment score is computed, e.g. "manipulative minus non-manipulative", or null.
fields.instruction: Write how the difference/discernment score is computed, e.g. 'manipulative minus non-manipulative'. Null when the DV is not a difference score. The veracity of the two components decides the sign of dv_polarity.

fields.name: dv_polarity
fields.label: DV Polarity
fields.description: 1=higher score is better/protective, 0=higher score is worse, null=not applicable.
fields.instruction: 1 = higher is better/protective, 0 = higher is worse, null = not applicable. fields.name: m1i_post

fields.name: sd1i_post

fields.name: m2i_post

fields.name: sd2i_post

fields.name: sd1i
fields.label: SD Group 1

fields.instruction: Part of the 'descriptives' effect route (n1i, m1i, sd1i, n2i, m2i, sd2i) - the preferred, always poolable route. The SD of group 1 at the tested timepoint.

fields.name: n2i

fields.name: m2i

fields.name: t_val
fields.label: t Statistic
fields.description: Exact t-test statistic.
fields.instruction: Part of the 't' effect route: t_val + (n1i and n2i, or n_total). A balanced two-arm design may give only n_total (n1 = n2 = n_total / 2).

fields.name: F_val
fields.label: F Statistic
fields.description: Exact F-statistic.
fields.instruction: Part of the '1-df F' effect route: F_val + df_num + df_den + (n1i and n2i, or n_total). Only df_num == 1 is a two-arm contrast.

fields.name: df_num
fields.label: df Numerator
fields.description: Numerator df for F-tests.
fields.instruction: The numerator df of the F test - part of the '1-df F' effect route. df_num > 1 means a multi-df omnibus: it compares more than two cells at once, cannot be signed, and must never be converted into a single two-arm d nor be the eligible primary effect.

fields.name: df_den
fields.label: df Denominator
fields.description: Denominator df for F-tests.
fields.instruction: The denominator df of the F test - part of the '1-df F' effect route (F_val + df_num + df_den + n).

fields.name: z_val
fields.label: z Statistic
fields.description: Exact z statistic (e.g. logistic/ordinal regression).
fields.instruction: The exact z statistic the paper reports (e.g. logistic or ordinal regression). It is not one of the eight effect routes on its own: report it, but the row still needs a route it can be pooled by.

fields.name: chi2_val
fields.label: Chi-square Statistic
fields.description: Exact chi-square statistic.
fields.instruction: The exact chi-square statistic the paper reports. A multi-df chi2 is an omnibus: it is never the eligible primary effect and must not be converted into a single two-arm effect.

fields.name: r_val
fields.label: r Correlation
fields.description: Exact correlation coefficient.
fields.instruction: Part of the 'r' effect route: r_val + n_total.

fields.name: n_total
fields.label: Total N
fields.description: Total N for correlation/statistical fallback conversions.
fields.instruction: Part of the 't' and 'r' effect routes (t_val + n_total, r_val + n_total), and the fallback for a balanced two-arm design, where n1 = n2 = n_total / 2. A DV row with no complete effect route must carry a non-empty missing_metrics_reason.

fields.name: beta_val
fields.label: Regression Beta
fields.description: Unstandardized or standardized regression coefficient (state which in conversion_method).
fields.instruction: Part of the 'regression coefficient' effect route: beta_val + (beta_se, sei or vi) or n_total.

fields.name: beta_se
fields.label: Regression Beta SE

fields.instruction: The standard error of the regression coefficient - part of the 'regression coefficient' effect route.

fields.name: log_odds
fields.label: Log Odds

fields.instruction: The log-odds coefficient the paper reports.

fields.name: odds_ratio
fields.label: Odds Ratio

fields.label: Odds Ratio CI Low

fields.instruction: The lower bound of the odds-ratio confidence interval - part of the 'odds ratio' effect route.

fields.name: or_ci_high

fields.instruction: The upper bound of the odds-ratio confidence interval - part of the 'odds ratio' effect route.

fields.name: risk_ratio
fields.label: Risk Ratio
fields.description: Risk ratio.
fields.instruction: The risk ratio the paper reports.

fields.name: p_val
fields.label: p Value

fields.name: p_censored

fields.name: eta2_p
fields.label: Partial Eta Squared

fields.name: eta2_p_ci_low
fields.label: Partial Eta Squared CI Low
fields.description: Lower bound of the partial eta-squared CI.
fields.instruction: The lower bound of the partial eta-squared confidence interval.

fields.name: eta2_p_ci_high
fields.label: Partial Eta Squared CI High
fields.description: Upper bound of the partial eta-squared CI.
fields.instruction: The upper bound of the partial eta-squared confidence interval.

fields.name: d_val
fields.label: Cohen's d

fields.name: g_val

fields.name: g_se
fields.label: g SE

fields.name: vi

fields.name: sei

fields.name: effect_size_type_reported
fields.label: Effect Size Type Reported

fields.name: effect_favors

fields.name: conversion_inputs

fields.name: missing_metrics_reason

fields.name: source_location
fields.label: Source Location

fields.name: source_quote

Copy it word for word from the paper or Text/<Key>.txt - do not paraphrase it; it must be findable in the text after whitespace normalisation. If the quote cannot be found, shorten it to a contiguous phrase and retry; if it crosses a page break or sits in an image-only table, quote the table caption or the sentence that introduces the table.

fields.name: source_span
fields.label: Source span (PDF rectangle)
fields.description: The page and the normalised rectangles of the passage the source quote was taken from.
fields.instruction: The page and the normalised rectangles of the passage the source quote was taken from - the object printed by `python Scripts/mark_source.py "<Study Key>" "<quote>"`, added verbatim. Every DV needs one; if a DV is genuinely unmarkable (no extractable text), say why in missing_metrics_reason and Rationale_Notes and leave the best span you can (caption or heading). Check that the page and the rectangles are sensible before moving on.

fields.instruction: 1 = a broad platform peer group, 2 = a national/fellow-citizen group, 3 = ideological in-group peers, 4 = unspecified/generic social consensus, 5 = a local community.

fields.name: Delivery_Format
fields.label: Presentation Format
fields.description: 1=Statistical normative statement/banner, 2=Simulated social counter/ upvote ratio, 3=Peer comment feedback prompt, 4=Interactive norm elicitation task.
fields.instruction: 1 = a statistical normative statement/banner, 2 = a simulated social counter or upvote ratio, 3 = a peer comment feedback prompt, 4 = an interactive norm elicitation task.

fields.name: Primary_Target_Variable
fields.label: Primary Behavioral / Cognitive Outcome
fields.description: 1=Sharing intentions, 2=Belief in misinformation, 3=Flagging/reporting suspicious content, 4=Discernment score.
fields.instruction: 1 = sharing intentions, 2 = belief in misinformation, 3 = flagging/reporting suspicious content, 4 = a discernment score.

fields.name: Ingroup_Congruence
fields.label: In-group Congruence of Norm Source
fields.description: 1=Ideological in-group source, 2=Out-group/general source, 3=Not applicable, null=Unclear.
fields.instruction: 1 = an ideological in-group source, 2 = an out-group/general source, 3 = not applicable, null = unclear.

platform_exposure_reduction.label: Platform Exposure Reduction / Downranking
platform_exposure_reduction.description: Platform- or system-level interventions that reduce, downrank, demote, or remove low-quality or untrustworthy content (feed algorithm changes, exposure-reduction field experiments, deplatforming). Use with the common core.

fields.name: Exposure_Mechanism
fields.label: Exposure Mechanism
fields.description: 1=Downranking/demotion in feed or search, 2=Removal/deletion of content, 3=Deplatforming/account removal, 4=Reduced distribution/reach, 5=Warning interruption before exposure, 6=Other.
fields.instruction: 1 = downranking/demotion in feed or search, 2 = removal/deletion of content, 3 = deplatforming/account removal, 4 = reduced distribution/reach, 5 = a warning interruption before exposure, 6 = other.

fields.name: Platform
fields.label: Platform
fields.description: Platform or system (e.g. "Facebook", "Instagram", "Search", "YouTube"), or null.
fields.instruction: A free-text field: name the platform or system, e.g. 'Facebook', 'Instagram', 'Search', 'YouTube'. Leave it empty when the paper does not name one - never invent a value.

fields.name: Targeting_Rule
fields.label: Targeting Rule
fields.description: 1=Untrustworthy sources/domains, 2=False content items, 3=Engagement/reach threshold, 4=Universal exposure limit, 5=Other.
fields.instruction: 1 = untrustworthy sources/domains, 2 = false content items, 3 = an engagement/reach threshold, 4 = a universal exposure limit, 5 = other.

fields.name: Assignment_Level
fields.label: Assignment Level
fields.description: 1=User-level randomization, 2=Cluster/geography randomization, 3=Platform-wide policy, 4=Natural experiment, 5=Other.
fields.instruction: 1 = user-level randomization, 2 = cluster/geography randomization, 3 = a platform-wide policy, 4 = a natural experiment, 5 = other.

fields.name: Content_Harm_Level
fields.label: Content Harm Level
fields.description: 1=Low-quality/untrustworthy, 2=False/misleading, 3=Harmful, 4=Mixed, null=Unclear.
fields.instruction: 1 = low-quality/untrustworthy, 2 = false/misleading, 3 = harmful, 4 = mixed, null = unclear.

generic.label: Generic Misinformation Intervention
generic.description: Misinformation/media-literacy interventions that are not primarily psychological inoculation or source-evaluation training, e.g. debunking corrections, media-literacy lessons, accuracy nudges, fact-checking training, open-mindedness interventions, or platform exposure-reduction experiments. Use with the common core (common.yaml).

fields.name: Theory_Basis
fields.label: Theory Basis
fields.description: Theory the intervention is based on (e.g. "inoculation theory", "elaboration likelihood", "motivated reasoning", "none stated"), or null.
fields.instruction: A free-text field: name the theory the intervention is based on (e.g. 'inoculation theory', 'elaboration likelihood', 'motivated reasoning') or write 'none stated'. Never invent a source.

fields.name: Intervention_Delivery
fields.label: Intervention Delivery
fields.description: 1=Direct Instruction, 2=Interactive/Practice, 3=Game-based, 4=Other.
fields.instruction: 1 = direct instruction, 2 = interactive/practice, 3 = game-based, 4 = other.

fields.name: Message_Timing
fields.label: Message Timing
fields.description: 1=Pre-exposure/prebunking, 2=Concurrent, 3=Post-exposure/debunking, 4=Mixed.
fields.instruction: 1 = pre-exposure/prebunking, 2 = concurrent, 3 = post-exposure/debunking, 4 = mixed.

fields.name: Correction_Scope
fields.label: Correction Scope
fields.description: 1=Specific claim, 2=Technique/generalizable, 3=General/abstract, 4=Other.
fields.instruction: 1 = a specific claim, 2 = technique/generalizable, 3 = general/abstract, 4 = other.

fields.name: Intervention_Components
fields.label: Intervention Components
fields.description: Array of applicable strings: ["Correction", "Warning", "Skills training", "Feedback", "Nudge", "Platform downranking/exposure reduction", "Community messaging"].
fields.instruction: A list-valued field: mark a passage that supports the listed values - the components the intervention combined, e.g. ['Correction', 'Warning', 'Skills training'].

sourcing.label: Sourcing / Source Evaluation
sourcing.description: Studies of sourcing and source-evaluation training interventions, typically lateral reading, click restraint, CRAAP/checklist evaluation, or fact-checking strategies that teach participants to evaluate the credibility of sources and online information. Use with the common core (common.yaml).

fields.name: Source_Eval_Strategy
fields.label: Source Evaluation Strategy
fields.description: The strategy taught - e.g. "lateral reading", "click restraint", "source-checking", "fact-checking site use", "CRAAP".
fields.instruction: A free-text field: name the source-evaluation strategy taught, e.g. 'lateral reading', 'click restraint', 'CRAAP'. Leave it empty when the paper does not state one - never invent a value.

fields.name: Assessment_Format
fields.label: Assessment Format
fields.description: 1=Quantitative rating scales, 2=Multiple-choice/forced-choice, 3=Open response/qualitative, 4=Mixed.
fields.instruction: 1 = quantitative rating scales, 2 = multiple-choice/forced-choice, 3 = open response/qualitative, 4 = mixed.

lateral_reading_and_verification.1: Technique-adoption paradigm (authentic web evaluation with screen recording/digital trace)

lateral_reading_and_verification.3: Both/Mixed. Sourcing = leaving the text to assess author/publisher credibility via third-party sources

sourcing.3: Both/Mixed. Sourcing = leaving the original text to assess credibility of authors/publisher via third-party sources

Interventions.label: Intervention arms
Interventions.description: One entry per arm of the experiment; each arm carries its own type and may override the record's field values.
